primary.title: Notes on Nursing: What It Is, and What It Is Not
primary.author: Florence Nightingale
primary.rationale: Nightingale's seminal work outlining her principles of nursing care and sanitation. It is widely considered a foundational text in modern nursing.

primary.title: Notes on Hospitals
primary.author: Florence Nightingale
primary.rationale: This work details Nightingale's observations and recommendations regarding hospital design, sanitation, and administration, drawing heavily from her Crimean War experiences.

primary.title: Cassandra
primary.author: Florence Nightingale
primary.rationale: A powerful essay written by Nightingale in her early twenties, critiquing the limited opportunities for educated women and advocating for their intellectual and professional development.

secondary.title: Florence Nightingale: A Life
secondary.author: Mark Bostridge
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and highly acclaimed biography of Florence Nightingale, based on extensive archival research. It is considered a definitive scholarly work on her life and impact.

secondary.title: Florence Nightingale and the Founding of Modern Nursing
secondary.author: Laura R. Creighton
secondary.rationale: This scholarly book examines Nightingale's contributions to nursing, focusing on her organizational skills, statistical methods, and advocacy for public health.

secondary.title: Florence Nightingale's Statistical Methods
secondary.author: Michael E. Caswell
secondary.rationale: An academic article that delves into Nightingale's pioneering use of statistics in public health and hospital reform, highlighting her innovative approaches to data visualization.

suggestions.notes: Florence Nightingale's extensive writings and correspondence provide a rich source for historical research on 19th-century healthcare, sanitation, and the role of women in public life. Her statistical work is particularly noteworthy.
